title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The incident involves a Minnesota lawyer who was suspended in connection with fake case citations attributed to AI use. This places the failure at the point where AI-generated legal research was submitted as authoritative court material, a context in which fabricated citations, a known failure mode of large language models, can cause direct procedural harm.

What is not established is any detail about which AI system was used, how many citations were affected, what court was involved, or the precise terms and duration of the suspension, because the underlying article text was not available to the source that reported on it.

The incident belongs to a pattern in which AI output asserting false information as fact is passed into a high-stakes professional process without verification. A human review step, standard in legal practice before AI tools became common, would in principle have been sufficient to catch citations that do not correspond to real cases.
